citation: Ciranka, Bahrami & van den Bos (2022) — Uncertainty drives social information use in risky choice across adolescence

source.note: Adapted to jsPsych v8 from Ciranka et al.'s jsPsych v6 implementation (Z_Experiment_Code/index.html plus Z_Experiment_Code/jspsych-6.0/CiriPlugins/*). v1 port keeps only the description-format risky-choice trials (condition 3 in the original); the original task additionally includes a sampling/experience condition and a social-advice condition that we defer to v2. Probability set, payoff set, and the two excluded payoff combinations match the source verbatim.

description: Forced choice between a SAFE option (5 points guaranteed) and a RISKY option (probability p of winning V points, otherwise 0). Six probability levels and three payoff levels are crossed factorially with two combinations excluded; remaining 16 unique trials are repeated 4 times each (64 total trials). Tests risk aversion, expected-value sensitivity, and the magnitude-by-probability interaction.
